summary: Three generalized answer-bank profiles reveal the correct first operation through coefficient frequency. The shortcut survives UI shuffling and delivery filtering. Other checks passed; the package remained unchanged.

source_analysis.skill: Identify two row additions that create zeros in one column of a 3x3 matrix using the specified pivot row.
reasoning_steps: Identify the pivot row and cleared column.
Calculate each target row’s cancellation coefficient.
Verify both operations across the complete rows.
invariants: Two row additions using one unchanged pivot row.
Five-choice radio response with one correct pair.
permitted_variations: Distractor roles and ordering without predictable answer-bearing assignments.

source_replay.details: Reproduced all ten complete source banks and canonical matrices/operations. Source correct designations match. The canonical example has no captured answer bank.

math.details: Independently checked 153 records using exact integer arithmetic, including every choice and both solution stages.

variety.details: Covered all ten profiles, four coefficient-sign combinations and nine pivot/column coordinates. Numerical variety passes; decision-relevant bank variation fails separately.

scope.details: Preserves the easy two-operation workload and response contract. Unsupported difficulties are rejected.

grading.details: Native grader correctly accepted 153 independently verified choices and rejected 612 distractors. Additional shortcut submissions behaved as predicted.

rendering.details: Actual UI screenshots inspected for batch and controlled variations. Long solution chains remain accessible through horizontal scrolling. UI reordering refuted the initial positional-shortcut hypothesis.

packaging.details: Exact dependency versions, deterministic replay, relocation and rejection cases passed. Package hashes are unchanged.

decision_variation.details: The modal first coefficient reveals the correct first operation in 36/36 fresh cue-positive records, 24/24 delivered fresh survivors and both affected runner-batch survivors. Captured inventory contains only original source questions, with no stored generated records.

findings.description: Profiles q-42531, q-130451 and q-91162 always retain the correct first coefficient in their extra unit-coefficient distractor. Consequently, that signed coefficient appears three times while its negation appears twice. Learners can recover the first operation without inspecting the matrices and calculate only the second. This order-independent shortcut affects two surviving records in the exact five-record batch.
findings.reproduction: Run the context Python with `-B reproduce_shortcut.py` from evidence_root; expected exit 1. Minimal case: profile=q-42531, seed=472, A=[[1,2,3],[2,5,4],[-3,7,8]], pivot=0, column=0, ks=[0,-2,3]. Bank pairs are [(-2,-1),(2,-3),(-2,3),(-2,-3),(2,3)]. Frequency reveals -2; calculating only the second coefficient selects the accepted pair (-2,3). See counterfactual-records.json and shortcut-grader-report.json.
findings.requested_change: Revise generalized unit-perturbation recipes so the extra distractor does not invariably preserve the correct first coefficient. Vary eligible coefficient roles and signs while preserving distinct choices, source replay and the two-operation skill. Retain the reproduction as a regression, verify the predictor fails across recognizable bank subgroups after delivery, and regenerate the candidate batch. Do not remove source families or modify original inventory questions.
